findings.problem: Breaks the 12 px stage margin rule: at rest the three chain blocks sit at stage x 0 / 333 / 666 (each 270 wide) and y 10, so block 1's left edge and block 3's right edge are flush with the stage edges (0 px margin) and the cards start 10 px from the top. Scene 8 draws the very same chain at x 12 / 333 / 654 (y 40), so the chain also jumps 12 px sideways between scenes 8 and 10. The pop-in spring overshoots further outside the stage (about -4 px).
findings.fix: In the BLK constants use x0 = 12 and step 321 (blocks at 12 / 333 / 654, right edge 924, the same as scene 8) and y = 12. The elbow links then span 51 px, the gap scene 8 already fits its tick discs into; the work bars (y 334 and below) and the legend tags are unaffected.
findings.evidence: Measured at 111.7 s (scene 10, local 9.5): v-card rects [0,10,270,290], [333,10,603,290], [666,10,936,290] against stage 936 x 640; scene 8 at 87.2 s: [12,40,282,266], [333,40,603,266], [654,40,924,266]. Full-video sweep (every 0.25 s) shows the same persistent violation from 102.55 s to 112.8 s. Stills algo-8-s10-3.png and s10-9.png: block 1's left border and block 3's right border sit on page x 72 and 1008.

findings.scene: common-3.js (A8.chars marks, A8.block field labels; seen in scenes 7, 8, 9 and 10)
findings.problem: Marked hex digits are drawn as -ink text on the saturated EDGE colour (background var(--c-edge), color var(--c-ink)). Measured contrast is 3.36:1 for the red marks, 3.64:1 for the green and the orange marks, below the 4.5:1 the -ink shades are meant to reach (they only reach it on white or on their own light -dim tint, not on the edge colour). The marked digits are the point of scenes 7 and 8 (which digits differ or match) and of the first-digit check in scenes 9 and 10. Smaller issue: the block field labels (prev / hash / nonce, var(--text-dim) grey) on the red-tinted prev strip of a broken block reach only 4.28:1.
findings.fix: In chars() use color var(--c-on) on the var(--c-edge) mark: the -on shades give 9.1:1 (green #173a00 on #a5ed6e), 9.5:1 (red #450707 on #ffb2b2) and 10.6:1 (orange #3d2000 on #ffd28a), the same -on rule as every solid sticker. Alternatively keep the -ink text and switch the mark background to the light var(--c-dim) tint. For the labels, give the strip's label var(--c-ink) when the strip is red (rose-ink on rose-dim is 4.63:1).
findings.evidence: Computed-colour scan of every text node, sampled every 0.25 s over the whole video (steady state, opacity > 0.97): rgb(203,20,20) on rgb(255,178,178) = 3.36 (338 samples, scenes 8-10); rgb(65,124,0) on rgb(165,237,110) = 3.64 (600 samples, scenes 7-10); rgb(159,94,0) on rgb(255,210,138) = 3.64 (190 samples, scenes 7, 8, 10); rgb(107,107,107) on rgb(255,223,224) = 4.28 (31 samples, scenes 8, 10). Every other text/background pair in the video is at least 4.6:1. Stills algo-8-s7-7.png (orange marks), s8-7.png (red marks), s9-3.png.

findings.problem: The six captions carry typed numbers ('5 and 11', 'n = 55', 'z = (5 - 1) x (11 - 1) = 40', 'e = 3 ... 40', 'd = 27, because 3 x 27 = 81 = 2 x 40 + 1', '(55, 3) ... 27') while every on-screen row of the same scene is built from A8.RSA and asserted. House rule: numbers come from the helpers and are asserted, never typed. Scenes 4, 6 and 9 already build their captions from the data (template strings over D / R / M), so scene 5 is the one place where a changed key pair would leave the captions silently wrong.
findings.fix: Build the captions from R and the row strings (the file already has R and TX), e.g. `Pick two secret primes: ${R.p} and ${R.q}.`, `Multiply them: n = ${R.n} will be public.`, `Next ${TX.zHead} = ${R.z}, kept secret.`, `Pick e = ${R.e}: it shares no factor with ${R.z}.`, `d = ${R.d}, because ${TX.relMain} ${TX.relLast}.` and `Publish (${R.n}, ${R.e}). Keep ${R.d} secret.`
findings.evidence: Source lines 258-264 (plain string literals) against lines 55-90 where the row texts are built from R. No visual difference today: the typed values equal the asserted ones (stills algo-8-s5-3.png to s5-11.png).

findings.problem: The caption 'Checking takes just 1.' (7.3-8.4 s) has a number with no unit: the sentence stops after '1'. The on-screen bar says 'check: 1 hash', so the word is available, but a first-time learner reading only the caption meets 'just 1.' and has to guess what is counted (hashes, seconds, tries).
findings.fix: Make the template `Checking takes just ${M.checkCost} hash.` (the number still comes from M.checkCost, which is 1) or, to read better with the previous caption, `Checking it takes just ${M.checkCost} hash.`
findings.evidence: Source line 255: `Checking takes just ${M.checkCost}.`; stills algo-8-s9-7.5.png and s9-8.png (E folder) show the caption 'Checking takes just 1.' under the bar labelled 'check: 1 hash'.

findings.problem: Alice and Bob are placed at y 48 (as in the storyboard), which leaves a 10 px top margin; scenes 3-6 place the same discs at y 50 and keep the 12 px margin. Left and right margins are 14 px.
findings.fix: Use y: 50 for A8.person alice and bob (the wire label, wire and message row sit well below, so nothing else moves). The storyboard's y 48 for scene 2 can be corrected at the same time.
findings.evidence: Stage-relative rects of the two v-gene discs at rest: scene 2 [14,10,90,86] and [846,10,922,86]; scene 3 at 20 s [14,12,90,88] and [846,12,922,88]. Still algo-8-s2-3.png.

findings.problem: In the odds figure the orange ring round the 16 x 16 square starts at stage y 119.0, while the 'one square, one hash' label ends at y 119.2 and its 4 px lip runs to 123.2, so the ring's top border runs through the label's lip: the label looks stuck to the ring instead of sitting above it.
findings.fix: Move the label up by 10 px (label y = GRID.y - 46) or push the square and its ring (and, for alignment, the odds tags) down by 10 px; the grid still ends well inside the stage (ring bottom 521 + 10).
findings.evidence: Measured at local 12.5 s: ring top 119.0 and bottom 521.0, label top 68.8 and bottom 119.2 with box-shadow 0 4px 0. Stills algo-8-s9-11.png and E/algo-8-s9-12.5.png show the ring touching the label.

findings.problem: The literal paint colours collide with the video's colour roles: Alice's secret paint is the exact red token that means 'Eve / broken' everywhere else and sits beside Eve's red dashed frames and arrows; Bob's blue paint is the 'public' blue inside a purple 'secret' frame; the orange and green mixtures are the 'attention' and 'valid' colours. The tan result of the three paints (an average of the tokens) is the one colour that is not in the CSLingo palette. The storyboard accepts this, but a first-time learner may read the red pot as Eve's.
findings.fix: Optional: make the frame, not the paint, carry the meaning. Give the secret pots a solid 3 px purple frame (not dashed) with the 'secret' tag directly under each pot, and keep Eve's red dashed frames visibly different (dashed, smaller pots, a red eye above). A change of paint to non-role tokens is not possible within the palette, so documenting the exception in the scene 3 header comment (it already says paints are literal colours) is enough.
findings.evidence: Stills algo-8-s3-5.png (red and blue secret pots), s3-7.png and s3-9.png (red Eve frames beside the red pot), s11-5.png and s11-8.9.png (tan pots).
